_how_to_use: The featured hero (section 2) always shows the most recent episode whose status is 'released' or 'dropping_soon'.
Every other 'released' episode appears in the episode index (section 3) with a WATCH link.
video.mp4 / video.poster are paths inside site/public/ (e.g. 'media/lwa_s1e01_the_flip.mp4').
After editing, run:  python3 site/build.py   then commit and deploy.
Optional index_name / index_teaser: shorter text for the episode-index row; otherwise name / teaser are used.

Optional video.mp4_3d (+ optional video.poster_3d): the 3D equipment panel (pipeline/hx3d.py, 960x1080, same length as the episode). When set, the featured card shows it to the right of the 2D video, playing in step.
Optional video.vtt: captions file inside site/public/ (put it in site/static/captions/, e.g. 'captions/lwa_s1e01_the_flip.vtt').

episodes.subject: Heat Transfer
episodes.name: Heat Transfer — The Flip
episodes.question:
“Same exchanger. Same fluids.
Flip the flow — why does heat transfer jump?”
episodes.teaser: Same exchanger. Flip one stream. Why does heat transfer jump?
episodes.summary: A shell-and-tube heat exchanger runs two ways. Parallel flow. Countercurrent flow. The geometry is identical. So why is countercurrent almost always better — and by how much?
episodes.figure_caption: FIG. 1 — SHELL & TUBE EXCHANGER · COUNTERCURRENT FLOW

episodes.title: The Fouling Problem
episodes.subject: Heat Transfer
episodes.name: The Fouling Problem
episodes.teaser: Your exchanger was designed clean. Six months later it moves less heat. Where did that resistance come from — and how do engineers account for it?
episodes.index_teaser: Your exchanger was designed clean. As deposits build up, heat transfer can fall—where does the extra resistance come from?
episodes.question:
“Designed clean. Six months later, less heat.
Where did the extra resistance come from?”
episodes.summary: A deposit just 0.08 mm thick adds a resistance in series with the tube wall and the two films. U falls about 17%, the outlets drift, and the exchanger moves about 6% less heat.

episodes.title: Baffles — What They Do and Why They Matter
episodes.subject: Heat Transfer
episodes.name: Baffles — What They Do and Why They Matter
episodes.index_name: Baffles — What They Do and Why
episodes.teaser: Without baffles, shell-side fluid would short-circuit straight through. How a segmental plate forces the fluid into a zig-zag path, and what that does to heat transfer and pressure drop.
episodes.index_teaser: Without baffles, shell-side fluid short-circuits. How a plate forces a meandering path — and changes shell-side flow and heat transfer.

episodes.title: Which Fluid Goes Inside the Tubes?
episodes.subject: Heat Transfer
episodes.name: Which Fluid Goes Inside the Tubes?
episodes.index_name: Which Fluid Goes Inside the Tubes?
episodes.teaser: Corrosive? High pressure? Viscous? There is a decision rule — and breaking it costs you in maintenance or efficiency. Here is the logic engineers actually use.
episodes.index_teaser: Corrosive? High pressure? Viscous? There is a decision rule — and breaking it costs you in maintenance or efficiency.

episodes.title: Your Kettle Has the Same Problem as a Refinery
episodes.subject: Heat Transfer
episodes.name: Your Kettle Has the Same Problem as a Refinery
episodes.index_name: Your Kettle Has the Same Problem as a Refinery
episodes.teaser: Nucleate boiling, film boiling, Leidenfrost. The same phase-change physics that ruins a kettle operates at every reboiler in a refinery — and knowing the curve saves equipment.
episodes.index_teaser: Nucleate boiling, film boiling, Leidenfrost — the same curve that ruins a kettle operates at every reboiler in a plant.

episodes.subject: Process Safety
episodes.name: When a Tube Bursts
episodes.teaser: One tube splits inside a running exchanger. The high-pressure fluid floods the other side. What protects the shell, and why engineers design for a failure they hope never happens.
episodes.index_teaser: A tube splits inside a running exchanger. What protects the shell from the high-pressure side?

episodes.subject: Instrumentation & Control
episodes.name: Holding the Outlet Temperature
episodes.teaser: Feed changes, fouling grows, weather shifts, yet the outlet must stay on target. How a control loop and a bypass keep an exchanger steady.
episodes.index_teaser: Everything upstream changes. How does a control loop keep the outlet on target?

episodes.subject: Mass Transfer
episodes.name: The Exchanger Under the Column
episodes.teaser: Every distillation column hides a heat exchanger at its base. Why the reboiler is where separation really begins, and the start of our next mystery: the column.
episodes.index_teaser: Every distillation column hides an exchanger at its base. Where separation really begins.
